questions.stem: What is the first requirement for natural selection to occur?

options.text: Organisms must be able to choose their mates
There must be variation within the population

questions.explanation: Natural selection requires variation within a population. Without differences between individuals, there would be no traits that give some organisms a survival advantage over others.

options.text: The force of gravity on an organism
An environmental factor that affects survival and reproduction
The number of offspring an organism produces
The rate at which mutations occur

questions.explanation: A selection pressure is an environmental factor that affects which organisms survive and reproduce. Examples include predation, competition for resources, disease, and climate changes.

questions.stem: How does antibiotic resistance develop in bacteria through natural selection?

options.text: Bacteria learn to resist antibiotics over time
Resistant bacteria survive antibiotic treatment and reproduce, passing on resistance alleles
Antibiotics cause bacteria to mutate and become resistant

questions.explanation: Some bacteria already carry resistance alleles due to random mutations. When antibiotics are used, non-resistant bacteria die while resistant ones survive and reproduce, passing on the resistance alleles. Over time, the resistant population increases.

questions.stem: What happens to the frequency of an advantageous allele in a population over time?
questions.explanation: An advantageous allele increases in frequency over time because organisms carrying it are more likely to survive and reproduce. As more offspring inherit the allele, it becomes more common in the population.

questions.stem: Why is the overuse of antibiotics a concern?

options.text: It causes humans to become resistant to bacteria
It increases the rate of natural selection for resistant bacteria

questions.explanation: Overuse of antibiotics increases the selection pressure for resistant bacteria. Each time antibiotics are used, resistant bacteria are selected for, leading to more antibiotic-resistant strains that are difficult to treat.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes adaptation?

options.text: An individual organism changing during its lifetime
A feature that helps an organism survive in its environment, developed through natural selection

questions.explanation: An adaptation is a feature or characteristic that has evolved through natural selection because it helps an organism survive and reproduce in its environment. Adaptations develop over many generations, not within a single lifetime.

questions.stem: Natural selection can eventually lead to the formation of new species. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Speciation is the formation of new species from existing ones. It occurs when populations become isolated and natural selection acts differently on each group, eventually leading to populations that can no longer interbreed.
